qs.q: A 32-year-old man with Crohn disease develops an enterocutaneous fistula. What pathological feature of this condition predisposes patients to deep tissue tracking and fistula formation compared to ulcerative colitis?
qs.e: Crohn disease is characterized by transmural inflammation that extends through all layers of the bowel wall, facilitating sinus tracts and fistulae. Ulcerative colitis is restricted primarily to superficial mucosal and submucosal layers, making fistulization rare.
